audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Graves and 2+ items to Camille, while the page's own whys[4] calls level 6 'her kill spike, not yours' and whys[6] says neither side clearly owns the late game.
audit.why: The sides contradicted the reasons printed directly beneath them, and the packet chart (Graves/Skill/Camille/Camille/Camille/Camille/Skill) agrees with the prose, not the sides.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Camille (3/10); 2+ items to Skill (5/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page keys off 'Hookshot's cooldown' without ever giving it, and one line invents a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s. Your own Collateral Damage is 100s at rank 1, so her ult is the longer clock and that is worth knowing at 6.
audit.corrected: Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 — that is the punish window. The Hextech Ultimatum is 140s at rank 1, forty seconds longer than your Collateral Damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three mechanical errors. Hookshot was called a stun in six places (it knocks up). Tactical Sweep was called a 'true-damage outer cone' twice (its outer half deals extra damage and heals her — no true damage). Camille was given 'E charges' she does not have. Adaptive Defenses was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's text: Hookshot knocks up on landing; Tactical Sweep's outer half slows, deals extra damage and heals; Q Precision Protocol is the only true-damage source in her kit; the passive shields her against the damage type that just hit her — which against Graves is physical, every time.
audit.corrected: Hookshot is a knockup off terrain, so fight away from walls. Only Precision Protocol's second cast is true damage; Tactical Sweep's outer half is extra damage plus her heal. And her first auto on you raises Adaptive Defenses, a shield built specifically against your physical damage, so the front of your burst is the part she absorbs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen was described as a blind that 'kills her follow-up auto weaving'.
audit.why: Graves' W reduces sight range and briefly slows on impact. It does not cause attacks to miss, so it never stopped her autos or her Q proc.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts her sight and slows her approach — it buys you the disengage, not immunity to her combo.

edits.before: Level 1 is your cleanest window — neither of you has a dash yet, so open with End of the Line to shove the wave and chunk her, and last-hit from max range where her short, single-target Q can't punish you back. The moment Camille picks up E, the lane tilts: her Hookshot dashes in and stuns on a wall, setting up Q's second-cast true-damage proc, and she heals off you with the true-damage outer half of her W cone. Don't walk up to throw a Q she can E-stun-punish — bait the Hookshot with a Quickdraw step instead, because its cooldown is long and she has almost no kill pressure without it.
edits.after: Level 1 is your cleanest window — neither of you has a dash yet, so open with End of the Line to shove the wave and chunk her, and last-hit from max range where her 325-range Q can't punish you back. The moment Camille picks up E the lane tilts: Hookshot pulls to a wall and knocks you up on landing, setting up Precision Protocol's second-cast true damage, and the outer half of Tactical Sweep heals her off you. Don't throw a Q she can answer — bait Hookshot with a Quickdraw step, because at 16s she has almost no kill pressure without it.

edits.before: This becomes her lane through levels 4-6. Her E charges and Q's true-damage second cast out-trade your True Grit armor stacking, and Smoke Screen's blind does nothing to slow her ability damage — it cuts her vision and zones her autos, but her Hookshot stun and Q proc land regardless. At 6, The Hextech Ultimatum walls you into a 1v1 the instant you're in range, locking down your Quickdraw dash-out. Drop Smoke Screen when she dives so the blind kills her follow-up auto weaving, but accept you're trading even at best — look to roam or call your jungler rather than try to solo her.
edits.after: This becomes her lane through levels 4-6. Hookshot at 16s and Q's true-damage second cast out-trade your True Grit stacking, and Smoke Screen does nothing to her ability damage — it cuts her sight and slows on impact, but the knockup and the Q proc land regardless. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum (140s) anchors you into a 1v1 the instant you're in range, shutting off your Quickdraw exit. Drop Smoke Screen when she dives so the slow buys you the disengage, but accept you trade even at best — roam or call your jungler rather than solo her.

notes: Three real mechanical errors fixed: Hookshot was called a stun throughout (Riot's text says it knocks up — that changes what tenacity does to it), Tactical Sweep was called a 'true-damage outer cone' (it is extra damage plus her heal; Precision Protocol is the only true damage in her kit), and Camille was credited with 'E charges' she does not have. Adaptive Defenses — a shield built against the damage type that just hit her, i.e. always physical against Graves — was absent from the page entirely and is now in whys[3] and wants.foe[2]. Packet suspectNames flagged 'Hold The Hextech Ultimatum' and 'Smoke Screen's' as wrong names: both are FALSE POSITIVES on the name, though the Smoke Screen line's 'blind' claim was wrong and is fixed. Per the mirrored Camille audit I ignored the kit's 'untargetable' and 'channel' flags on her R as tooltip-parse misfires. Packet games is only 27 here while the brief header says 1474; I did not lean on either win-rate figure.
